_comment: Town directory. Listings are free and always will be. RULES, kept here so they survive the person who wrote them: (1) An entry goes in only when its details have been checked live — a dead link is worse than a missing entry, same rule as report-it. (2) `checked` is the date that happened; it is printed, so rot is visible rather than silent. (3) Categories where local businesses compete for the same customer — food, trades, accommodation — stay OPEN rather than partly filled, because a partial list of cafes reads as a recommendation and this site takes no view on named businesses. Set `open: false` and populate only when the list is genuinely complete. (4) No ranking, no ratings, no reviews. Alphabetical within a category, and that is the whole editorial policy. Churches: St Columba's PARISH church (Church of Scotland, Gallowgate Street) is deliberately absent — the congregation united into Cumbrae, Fairlie & Largs and the building was sold, bid accepted February 2026. Do not re-add it from a directory site. The St Columba's that IS listed is the Scottish Episcopal church on Aubery Crescent, a different denomination in a different building. Churches, two traps recorded so they are not walked into again: (1) St Columba's PARISH church (Church of Scotland, Gallowgate Street) is gone — the congregation united into Cumbrae, Fairlie & Largs and the building was sold, bid accepted February 2026. The St Columba's that IS listed is the Scottish Episcopal church on Aubery Crescent: different denomination, different building. (2) Clark Memorial Church and Largs Community Church are THE SAME BUILDING on Bath Street. CFL's own site calls it Largs Parish Church; the town and the listed-building record call it Clark Memorial. Both names are in the entry so either search finds it. No service time is stated: CFL lists three times across three sites without saying which is which, and a wrong time sends someone to a locked door. Within a category, entries carry the same KINDS of detail. One entry with a phone number among five without reads as singled out, and the eye treats the difference as meaningful when it is not. If one gets a number, they all do, or none do.

entries.blurb: Lawn bowls club.

entries.name: Largs Inspire Badminton Club
entries.blurb: Badminton for children aged 5 to 13, at the Community Sport Hub.

entries.name: Largs TAGB
entries.blurb: Taekwondo, at the Community Sport Hub.

entries.name: Largs Table Tennis Club
entries.blurb: Table tennis for beginners and competitive players.

categories.blurb: Places to eat and drink in Largs.

categories.blurb: Places to stay in and around Largs.

categories.blurb: Rooms and halls in Largs available to book.

entries.name: Barrfields Theatre
entries.blurb: A 470-seat theatre at Vikingar!, available for hire through KA Leisure.

entries.name: Largs Community Sport Hub
entries.blurb: Two halls, seating around 250 and 350, bookable through KA Leisure.

entries.name: Largs Parish Church halls
entries.blurb: Halls and meeting spaces at the Bath Street church, with availability published online.

entries.name: Brisbane Evangelical Church
entries.blurb: An independent evangelical congregation on School Street.

entries.name: Largs Parish Church (Clark Memorial)
entries.blurb: Church of Scotland, part of the Cumbrae, Fairlie and Largs parish. The 1892 building on Bath Street is category A listed and holds a Grade 1 listed Father Willis organ. Sunday morning worship — see their site for the current time.

entries.name: Largs United Free Church
entries.blurb: United Free Church of Scotland congregation on Brisbane Road, near the fire station.

entries.name: St Columba's Scottish Episcopal Church
entries.blurb: Scottish Episcopal congregation at the corner of Aubery Crescent and Greenock Road, with 19th-century connections to Lord Kelvin.

entries.name: St Mary's Star of the Sea
entries.blurb: Roman Catholic church on Greenock Road, with a timber-clad gable and a granite statue of Our Lady.

categories.label: Sport & leisure
categories.blurb: Places to swim, play, train and watch sport in Largs.

entries.name: Largs Golf Club
entries.blurb: An 18-hole parkland course south of the town, established in 1891, with views over the Clyde to Cumbrae, Bute and Arran. Visitors welcome and tee times bookable online.

entries.name: Largs Thistle F.C.
entries.blurb: Founded in 1889 and playing in the West of Scotland League Premier Division, at Barrfields Park.

entries.name: Routenburn Golf Club
entries.blurb: Golf course above the town.

entries.name: sportscotland National Centre Inverclyde
entries.blurb: A residential sports training centre in 86 acres above the town, taking group bookings for facilities and organised activities.
entries.note: The golf training centre here closed permanently on 31 March 2026.

entries.name: Vikingar!
entries.blurb: A four-lane 25m pool and teaching pool, gym, the Viking Experience, Multiball and a café, alongside Barrfields Theatre. Run by KA Leisure.

categories.label: Sailing & marina
categories.blurb: Berthing, boatyards and sailing on the Largs Channel.

entries.name: Largs Sailing Club
entries.blurb: At the Yacht Haven. Dinghy racing, RYA training through the LSTA, and an active cruising section for sail and power. The Lookout Lounge has an honesty café open daily.

entries.name: Largs Yacht Haven
entries.blurb: Marina berthing, lifting and launching, dry berthing and a boatyard, on the shore south of the town.
